column1: # The slot and link trace for decision 0007 task 5, bullet 3.
# Tab-separated. The first column is the record kind.
#   cap      how many slots the main trace runs over. Small on purpose: the
#            original names MAXTHINKERS only in its overflow guard, so it runs
#            happily over shorter arrays as long as the trace never reaches
#            the end of them, and the whole state then fits in a comparison
#   exhaust  the capacity the exhaustion run uses. This one has to be the
#            original's own number, because exhaustion is the one place the
#            two capacities must be the same.
#   op       kind and two arguments (`-` where an operation takes fewer):
#              tremove  t    -      -- P_RemoveThinker, a mark, not an unlink
#            The rows are the trace, executed top to bottom, and all three
#            worlds run every one of them.
#   check    id, world (T or M), preloaded cells, the kernel, its scalar
#            arguments, an array to shorten, the status the CORE kernel must
#            return, how many cells the call changes, and why. These are NOT
#            part of the trace: each runs against a world of its own. A
#            SHORTENING names one array whose declared COUNT is one less than
#            the others' while the storage is the same size. Every kernel here
#            takes five counts and compares against the one it was given, and
#            without this they are five names for one number: `a >= n_func`
#            and `a >= n_next` would be the same program. `state` shortens to
#            one element, which puts the bump outside its own buffer.
#            HOW MANY CELLS THE CALL CHANGES is measured, not derived, and it
#            is here to be pinned rather than to be argued from. The ABI does
#            not promise that a refusal leaves the buffers as it found them --
#            a kernel may have written some of them before the access that
#            failed, and tadd-tail-past writes three. Declaring the number
#            makes that an observation instead of something nobody looked at,
#            and makes a change to it something to notice.
# THE THREE WAYS FULL AND CORE PART COMPANY, all pinned by pairs below.
#   Off the end of an array. A Ruby Array grows or reads nil; here it is
#   SPINEL_CORE_BOUNDS. Every declared buffer face of every kernel has a pair,
#   and each pair is the exact last index and the one after it.
#   BELOW the start of an array. This is the direction where the ORIGINAL is
#   not merely different but wrong: `remove_thinker(-1)` counts from the end in
#   Ruby and silently marks the LAST slot, which the next sweep then frees.
#   The kernel answers SPINEL_CORE_BOUNDS and writes nothing.
#   Outside what an i32 cell holds. `func` and `data` arrive as i64 because
#   that is what the ABI passes scalars in, and land in i32 arrays. CRuby
#   stores 2147483648 in `@th_func` without comment; the kernel answers
#   SPINEL_CORE_ARITHMETIC. The pairs below pin both ends of both fields.
# Status 1 (ARGUMENT) does not appear and cannot: it is about the pointers and
# counts the harness passes, which tests/core-boundary/buffers.sh covers.
# WHY `func` COUNTS UP FROM 10. The original's sweep distinguishes TH_REMOVED
# from everything else and nothing finer; its ten dispatch branches cover 0 to
# 9, so a live slot given 10 or more falls through all of them and the sweep
# runs with no thinker function called. That is what lets the ORIGINAL
# run_thinkers be driven here at all. Giving every slot TH_NULL would do it
# too, and would also let a kernel that ignored its `func` argument pass, so
# the values differ from each other instead. free_thinker puts a freed slot
# back to TH_NULL, which is 10, and that is the original's own behaviour.
# WHY THESE OPERATIONS. Slots 1, 2 and 3 are allocated by the bump allocator;
# 2 is marked and swept, and the next allocation gets 2 back AT THE TAIL of
# the list rather than where it was -- reuse is observable in the order, not
# only in the number. Then two slots are marked and swept together, and the
# next two allocations return them in the REVERSE of the order they were
# freed, because the free list is a stack and not a queue: a reference model
# that used a queue would disagree exactly here. Later the head, an interior
# slot and the tail are swept in one pass. The mobj side does the same without
# WHAT IS NOT HERE. Freeing one slot twice. The original permits it and so
# does the extraction -- both thread the slot to itself and hand it out twice
# -- but the model cannot represent it, because its free list is an Array and
# the second push is a second entry rather than an alias. It is a caller's
